selections.comment: Korroor won in this grade over 6f at Newcastle, despite hanging left in the closing stages, and could have a say in proceedings. However, IRISH DANCER looks to have the stronger form, having landed a handicap over the minimum trip at Catterick last month, and Declan Carroll's sprinter could prove the one to side with at this level. War Zone has won in classified company on the all-weather and could shape well on his belated turf debut.

selections.comment: A runner-up at Nottingham on his reappearance, ARCHIVIST can be considered unlucky not to have finished closer to the winner. The son of Dubawi failed to get a clear run at a crucial stage and has strong claims of going one better on only his second start for the William Haggas yard. Clouds Hill came up short when making a bold bid from the front at Musselburgh on his debut. He merits consideration, along with Silent Storm and New York Minute.

selections.comment: CHALK MOUNTAIN finished a strong third at Kempton on last month's reappearance. Stuart Kittow's charge may have done all his winning on the all-weather so far, but a short-head defeat at Newbury last summer offers encouragement he can come good on the turf, and he gets the vote. The application of blinkers should help Commanding Prince settle better and he can get involved, while better is expected from Liamarty Dreams in this lower grade.

selections.comment: MISS SHOW DOWN kept on into fourth despite looking outpaced at Goodwood on her return to action last month, having won from 4lb lower at Bath in September. The unexposed daughter of Showcasing should be suited by the stiff nature of this track and is expected to progress today, although Catterick scorer and previous C&D winner Tees Aggregates should make a good fist of things. The consistent Toolatetonegotiate can pick up some minor money.

selections.comment: Solanna deserves a change of luck having filled the runner-up spot on his last two starts but, although respected, the vote goes to TATMEEN. Beaten a neck over the mile on his handicap bow here in April before going one place better when upped to this trip at Kempton latest, there should be more to come and a 5lb rise might not be enough to halt his progress. Meleri is another to consider.

selections.comment: A difficult race to unpick with many of these having something to prove, so only a tentative vote can go to CASUAL ENCOUNTER. Andrew Balding's filly has made little impact in her three starts so far but she's a half-sister to City Spirit, who won over an extended 1m3f for these connections, and it is interesting that they opt for a classified contest over handicaps. The saddle slipped on Drouthy Neebor when having to be pulled up at Wolverhampton (sent off favourite) recently and could be worth another chance, while Jack Langley is also noted.

He offers the prospect of further improvement and Charlie Longsdon's five-year-old is taken to defy a 7lb rise. Beny Nahar Road is preferred to Jaitroplaclasse of the remainder.

selections.comment: BECTIVE ABBEY was having his first outing after wind surgery when successful in a handicap hurdle at Ffos Las. Nicky Henderson wastes no time in sending his unexposed charge over the larger obstacles and the seven-year-old can defy a 5lb rise in this lower grade. Do No Wrong returned the ready winner of this contest last year. He's a strong contender with Brian Hughes on board, while Jimmy The Digger is preferred of the other two.

selections.comment: A bumper winner between the flags, LADIES DAY finished a respectable third under rules at Warwick last month. The daughter of Yeats will be a lot wiser for that experience and Jack Andrews' 3lb allowance further helps her cause. Plumpton fourth Hard Market is a likely improver fitted with a tongue-strap for the first time, while Georgie's Malt showed some promise at Hexham without threatening the winner and could shape well.

Zarhanya remains unexposed and may benefit from this step up in trip, while Rubies Or Gold and Champetre complete the shortlist.

selections.comment: There has been no stopping TWO B TANNED, who made all under Tom Kiely-Marshall to complete a four-timer at Leicester recently. The 5lb penalty looks unlikely to halt further progress, but she will need to be alert if she is to secure an early advantage from a wide draw. Flaine (second) couldn't quite reel in the reopposing Romantic Spirit (winner) over C&D last time and the pair ought to go well again. Handicap debutant Luisa should not be overlooked either.

selections.comment: COLLUSION had it all to do approaching the furlong pole at Kempton last time out, but the Inns Of Court gelding kept on powerfully close home to land his hat-trick. Candy Warhol is just one more to consider.

An improved effort last time up in trip puts Ottoman in the mix, he was placed at Bath and the addition of first time cheekpieces can bring out further improvement. Abstract Art should come on for his latest run when placed at Wolverhampton after a 4-month absence, he wants further than the extended mile and is a threat on his return to turf this term.

Abstract Art should come on for his latest run when placed at Wolverhampton after a 4-month absence, he wants further than the extended mile and is a threat on his return to turf this term.

selections.comment: There are obvious chances for the two with experience here; Grand Echo drops in grade second time out having ran a fair debut at triple-figure odds in a competitive maiden over 5f, he has a big chance if handling the step up in trip. JACK THE TOOTH made a promising debut at Windsor over 6f, which looks to be the best form of the two and only has the extra 1f to step up to. Of the many debutants here Explosion looks the most promising on breeding, from high-class sprinter Showcasing. Others of note are Penhallam and Sovereign Lord.

selections.comment: PASTORAL WAY drops into Classified company for the first time in the hands of Danny Tudhope and should benefit for the drop down to 5f here, he's not quite seen out 6f for the last two starts. Korroor has obvious claims off the back of winning a similar event at Newcastle last time in first-time visor (retained), it's his first run over the minimum distance but was cruising 1f out last time. Irish Dancer has been much improved since the application of the tongue tie when winning at Catterick last month and is another well fancied to go well.

selections.comment: COMMANDING PRINCE has been a model of consistency in his opening five starts with two wins and two seconds, first-time blinkers are reached for here after being a bit keen at Ayr last time out and another big chance from an unchanged mark. Jungle Land is one of many in behind with chances in a tricky small field, the step up to 7f shouldn't be a problem with him keeping on well over 6f last three starts. Chalk Mountain has mainly been campaigned on AW and remains winless on turf, he has a chance of a place alongside Liamaty Dreams who was a shade unlucky at Chester in his penultimate start.

selections.comment: FLICKERING HALO got the run of the race at Newcastle but was always doing enough to win last time, he steps up in trip again here and holds leading claims from a 1lb rise. Squeezebox is expected to run him close back down in grade, he should strip fitter for his season opener at Doncaster when given too much to do after a 7-month absence, with Rossa Ryan taking the ride. Just An Hour will need to bounce back from a below par effort at Salisbury last time, perhaps the 6lb rise was too much to handle but after an impressive win at Nottingham prior is well respected.

selections.comment: Today could be the day for TOOLATETONEGOTIATE to get off the mark after hitting the frame in six of her last eight starts. Miss Show Down won her final start of 2024 and should come on for her latest run at Goodwood after an absence, with a drop in grade here.

selections.comment: A tight contest which can go to ARTAVIAN who was a heavy ground winner last autumn and shaped with promise on his reappearance where caught late by a well handicapped rival. If building on that effort he can get the better of the unexposed Tatmeen who was a 12f polytrack winner last time and has run well at this track in the past. Meleri is another in good form and arrives on his last winning mark so should hold every chance as well.

selections.comment: DROUTHY NEEBOR remains a maiden but he had been showing a consistent level of form until last time where something was amiss. His best recent efforts are on polytrack and he's entitled to be thereabouts if getting a stiff test down in trip. Veteran Foinix is on a long losing run but takes a big drop in grade and he's feared most ahead of Fen Tiger who went too fast on his reappearance but is well treated on these terms on his autumn middle distance form.

She is the biggest danger along with Master Of My Fate who won 4 times over the winter on aritifical surfaces and is now beginning to drop in the weights.

Though he has competition up front from the inconsistent Gower Prince he could be tough to peg back. If they set the race up for a strong stayer then the beneficiary could be Beny Nahar Road who has got his jumping together of late. Ideally he would want a bit further but the track and strong pace could play into his favour.

selections.comment: A tight contest where MONTREGARD may be able to follow up on his last time out success. He's only gone up 6lb for that but really showed the benefit of a visor and likely has more to offer on a sound surface. Do No Wrong proved he retained his ability with a point victory last time and was still going well before falling when last seen over fences under rules in the autumn. He could pose the biggest challenge ahead of Bective Abbey who was 2-4 over hurdles and likely has more to offer over fences for a top yard given his point form.

selections.comment: The pair of last time out winners Zucayan and ZENATO appeal most. The former was impressive last time and will appreciate the drying ground but he has shown all of his best form at Ludlow which is sharper than this venue. The latter was given a fine ride from the front at a sharp venue last time beating a very useful flat performer so now looks well treated back in a handicap and gets the verdict. Max Of Stars has been out of form for some time but can't be dismissed either having dropped a long way in the weights.

selections.comment: A weak race which could see OFF THE BENCH lose his maiden tag. He has been in better form than most of his rivals of late and may prefer this surface to the fast ground he encountered last time. Gorgeous Mr George has been struggling since his debut effort but his best form has come on tapeta and he could go close if getting back to the level of his debut form while Raavi isn't dismissed either on handicap debut. The addition of a visor may spark some improvement.

selections.comment: PESSOA has an excellent course record and was a touch unlucky last time going down by a nose after being forced wide. This slight drop in trip will suit given his previous win came at 7f and he can get the better of last time out C&D winner Royal Observatory. He overcame a slow start that day and should get a decent pace to aim at again courtesy of top weight Value Added. Veteran Snooze Lane has tumbled down the weights and looked in need of the run last time. If any of his ability remains he could complete the places.

selections.comment: CALIBOS has been steadily progressive in handicaps and is the one to beat if his stamina holds up. His latest placed effort on the turf has been franked by the pair who finished ahead of him and it's possible the cheekpieces deliver more. Battle Stride was disappointing last time but ran well over C&D previously and is likely capable of much better given his stable. He can pose the biggest challenge ahead of Captious Cantor who was too keen but not disgraced when midfield last time.

selections.comment: Veteran BIZARRE LAW has returned to form on the AW of late and remains thrown in on his best efforts. He's a C&D winner and the form of his latest runner up effort has been franked. Star Of Atlantis has won twice on the tapeta and neither the 7lb rise nor the drop back in trip should stop him remaining competitive. Multiple course winner Triggered has a poor strike rate of late but arrives in decent form and can make his presence felt once again.
